ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows that the outer frame is square PQRS, with side length 10 cm. Points N and M are on the top side SR, and the middle segment MN is labeled 6 cm. There are small squares near the four corners in the figure, and the problem states that they are congruent; there are also four unshaded isosceles triangles arranged around the middle gray shaded region. Reasoning: Use the total area minus the unshaded parts. The area of square PQRS is 10×10=100 cm². The length of the top side SR is 10 cm, the length of MN is 6 cm, and the total length of the remaining two segments SN and MR is 10−6=4 cm; from the congruence of the left and right small squares in the figure, each segment is 2 cm, so the side length of each small square is 2 cm, and the total area of the four small squares is 4×2²=16 cm². The four unshaded triangles in the figure are congruent; the upper triangle has MN=6 cm as its hypotenuse and is an isosceles right triangle, so the height to MN is 3 cm, and its area is (1/2)×6×3=9 cm². The total area of the four triangles is 4×9=36 cm². Shaded area = 100−16−36=48 cm².

In the diagram, $PQRS$ is a square of side $10\mathrm{~cm}$. The distance $MN$ is $6\mathrm{~cm}$. The square is divided into four congruent isosceles triangles, four congruent squares and the shaded region.
What is the area of the shaded region?

method.method_draft: Use area subtraction. From the image, note that N and M lie on the top side of square PQRS, with congruent small corner squares on the two remaining top segments SN and MR. Since the outer side is 10 cm and MN is 6 cm, each small square has side (10-6)/2 = 2 cm, so the four small squares have total area 4·2^2 = 16. The image shows the four unshaded triangular notches are congruent isosceles right triangles, with the top one having base MN = 6 cm as its hypotenuse; equivalently its altitude to MN is 3 cm. Thus each triangle has area 1/2·6·3 = 9 cm^2, and all four triangles total 36 cm^2. Subtract unshaded area from the 10 by 10 square: 100 - 16 - 36 = 48 cm^2.
